images.caption: Duffus Castle. This is a 14th century building on a site which was fortified by at least the 12th century. It is a motte-and-bailey castle, the motte being the artificial mound on which it stands (not to be confused with a moat, which is a defensive stretch of water around a castle!). The bailey is the outer yard, enclosed by a curtain wall. Originally it would have been surrounded by the Loch of Spynie, but today its perimeter is marked by a shallow ditch.
images.alt: Duffus Castle. This is a 14th century building on a site which was fortified by at least the 12th century. It is a motte-and-bailey castle, the motte being the artificial mound on which it stands (not to be confused with a moat, which is a defensive stretch of water around a castle!). The bailey is the outer yard, enclosed by a curtain wall. Originally it would have been surrounded by the Loch of Spynie, but today its perimeter is marked by a shallow ditch.

images.caption: Duffus Castle, from the East. Looking up the cobble-stoned road from the East perimeter of the castle, from the moat towards the main ruins.  The moat on the left and right of the bridge is still water-filled and surrounds the entire castle site.

images.filename: Duffus Castle, from the South-East - geograph.org.uk - 13964.jpg
images.caption: Duffus Castle, from the South-East. The remains of a motte and bailey castle, dating back to the 14th Century, replacing an earlier wooden castle. The castle is derelict, but significant remains have survived, including a deep moat around the perimeter.
